prompt.context: Your client CARE FIRST (CF) is a large hospital system, comprising 100 acute general medicine hospitals across the US employing over 200,000 people nationwide. CF's patient mix are covered by a variety of insurance providers, however, the majority of patients are covered by Medicare and Medicaid. In the last five years, CF has acquired 70 hospitals in rural regions, increasing the number of patients it serves by 40%. For the last 10 years, CF has been outsourcing their foodservice needs to one contract vendor, FoodXperts. FoodXperts handles all in-room patient dining, cafeteria, retail dining and employs all staff and management as they relate to foodservice in CF's hospitals. Due to policy changes and emphasis on value based care, patient satisfaction, measured through HCAHPS scores, is now factored into hospital reimbursement rates from Medicare and Medicaid. CF has recently seen a decline in their reimbursement rates and believes it may be due to the low quality food and service that FoodXperts has been providing. CF has decided to end their contract with FoodXperts at the end of the next year and to begin self-operating foodservices on their own. By making this shift, CF will have to replace all staff and management that has been employed by FoodXperts. CF is worried that CEOs at individual hospitals will not be invested in this decision and will likely push back to keep outsourcing foodservice at their individual hospitals.
prompt.question: CF has asked your team to help them in planning for the transition to self-operating foodservices across the entire hospital system and replacing FoodXperts management and staff. How would you assist CF through this large scale change?

clarifying_info.a: CF headquarters is located in New York and has hospitals across the US in both rural and urban areas. Most decisions are made centrally at headquarters but CEOs of individual hospitals have some flexibility to modify plans if they can prove that it will be better for their patients overall.

clarifying_info.q: How many FTE are employed by FoodXperts?
clarifying_info.a: 5% of employees at CF are currently under FoodXperts management and would leave at the end of the contract. There are 200,000 employees total, so CF will need to hire approximately 10,000 people across all hospitals.

clarifying_info.q: Has CF ever done something like this in the past?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, CF used to outsource healthcare technology to another vendor and decided to self-operate this division a few years ago. The decision was abrupt and they lost a lot of great talent from the current vendor due to poor messaging from leadership. Some CEOs of individual hospitals disagreed with the decision and have been wary of other changes mandated from headquarters.

clarifying_info.q: Why is this change taking place and what are the main objectives?
clarifying_info.a: The change is happening because of declining patient satisfaction scores (HCAHPS) and thus lower reimbursement from Medicare and Medicaid. The main objective is to have a smooth transition to self-operating foodservice in an effort to increase patient satisfaction and reimbursement rates across the system.

framework: Assess: Stakeholder Analysis — identify key stakeholders at each hospital (CEOs, foodservice managers, FoodXperts staff/management eligible for retention)

Assess: Change Impact Assessment — conduct forums with impacted stakeholders to surface concerns, especially drawing on lessons from the prior healthcare technology transition; document all procedural changes requiring hiring and communications

Design: Hiring Plan — work with hospital CEOs and foodservice managers to create a plan to retain management and staff currently employed by FoodXperts; develop plan with central HR to fill remaining gaps
Design: Communications Plan — document all communications to stakeholders specifying audience, message, frequency, vehicle, and due date
Design: Learning & Development — plan for onboarding, training, and future development needs for new employees

Design: Change Management / Change Agent Network — identify change agents/champions across hospitals to lead the new foodservice structure, serve as SMEs, and be main points of contact for questions and concerns
Deploy: Hiring — roll out hiring plan from central office; prioritize retaining high-quality talent from FoodXperts especially in rural hospitals where talent is scarce
Deploy: Communications — execute awareness-building communications to CEOs; deploy targeted retention messaging to FoodXperts staff
Deploy: Change Management — facilitate Change Network meetings; ensure all employees know the change agents are the go-to contacts so management can continue day-to-day activities
Optional: Pilot — consider a trial run with a small set of hospitals early on to gather learnings before full system rollout

questions.prompt: Who are the key stakeholders involved in this transition?
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies multiple stakeholder groups: CF headquarters leadership, individual hospital CEOs, FoodXperts management and staff (potential retention targets), CF central HR, and patients (indirectly via HCAHPS scores). Candidate should note the tension between central HQ directives and individual hospital CEO autonomy, and reference the historical precedent of the healthcare technology change.

questions.prompt: What phases would you propose to roll out the transition to self-operate foodservice?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose a structured phased approach: Assess (stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment) → Design (hiring plan, communications plan, L&D plan, change agent network) → Deploy (execute hiring, execute communications, facilitate change network meetings). A strong candidate also suggests a pilot with a small set of hospitals to generate learnings before full rollout.

questions.prompt: How many new employees will CF need to hire, and what staffing math supports this?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate: 200,000 total CF employees × 5% employed by FoodXperts = 10,000 FTEs that will leave at end of contract. CF must hire approximately 10,000 new foodservice employees across 100 hospitals, roughly 100 per hospital on average. Rural hospitals may face greater hiring challenges due to limited local talent pools.

math.answer: CF must hire approximately 10,000 new foodservice employees.

questions.prompt: What are the anticipated challenges you foresee?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: (1) CEO resistance / lack of buy-in at hospital level given prior bad experience with the technology transition; (2) risk of losing good FoodXperts talent if retention messaging is poor; (3) recruiting difficulty in rural markets; (4) maintaining foodservice quality and continuity during the transition window; (5) coordination complexity across 100 hospitals; (6) timeline pressure since the contract ends at year-end.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the anticipated challenges CF might face in this transition?

categories.name: Stakeholder Resistance
ideas: Hospital CEOs may push back given negative experience with the healthcare technology transition
Individual CEOs may lobby to continue outsourcing at their specific hospital
Lack of central vs. local alignment on transition timelines and approach

categories.name: Talent & Workforce
ideas: Risk of losing high-quality FoodXperts staff and management if retention messaging is delayed or poorly handled
Difficulty hiring 10,000 foodservice workers, especially in rural markets
Onboarding and training 10,000 new employees within a tight timeline

categories.name: Operational Continuity
ideas: Maintaining food quality and patient satisfaction during the transition to avoid further HCAHPS score declines
Managing the handoff of cafeteria, retail dining, and in-room patient dining simultaneously
Ensuring no service gaps between FoodXperts contract end and self-operated staff being fully trained

categories.name: Communications
ideas: Crafting differentiated messages for HQ, hospital CEOs, and FoodXperts staff
Managing uncertainty among FoodXperts employees before retention decisions are finalized

categories.name: Change Management
ideas: Building CEO investment and ownership in a centrally-mandated change
Establishing a Change Agent Network in 100 hospitals within a compressed timeline
Drawing lessons from the prior technology outsourcing transition to avoid repeating mistakes

recommendation: Recommend a phased Assess → Design → Deploy approach over the next 12 months leading up to the FoodXperts contract termination
Prioritize an early stakeholder engagement and change impact assessment, explicitly addressing CEO concerns rooted in the prior technology transition
Build a Change Agent Network of hospital-level champions to drive local buy-in and serve as go-to contacts during the transition
Develop a comprehensive hiring and retention plan targeting FoodXperts staff, with special focus on rural hospitals where talent is scarcer
Consider piloting the transition with a small subset of hospitals to refine the playbook before full rollout
risks: CEO resistance could slow adoption or lead to unauthorized continued outsourcing at individual hospitals
Loss of FoodXperts talent if retention outreach is delayed, especially in rural markets
Service quality disruption during transition could further depress HCAHPS scores and reimbursement rates in the short term
Timeline is tight — the contract ends at year-end and 10,000 hires plus full onboarding must be completed
next_steps: Conduct stakeholder analysis and change impact assessment within first 30 days
Identify and recruit Change Agents at each hospital
Launch communications plan targeting CEOs and FoodXperts staff simultaneously
Begin pilot transition at 2-3 hospitals within 3 months to generate learnings
Scale hiring and full rollout based on pilot insights
